## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

-- 141_reading_deferrals.sql
-- SCHEMA migration (T-079, AT-17; no data). A reading can be deferred on the record, and every deferred act lists with
-- its age from one view.
--
-- WHY. The owner (2026-09-18): a deferral is legitimate "so long as it runs eventually"; nothing in the repository
-- enforced or even measured it. A search not run and a source not mined each carried a deferral and a date; a source
-- not read had no deferred state, so "chosen not to read yet" could not be told from "nobody has looked", and no query
-- listed all of them with their age. What reaches the guidebook without it: a source whose full text is owed for a
-- parameter, deferred once, never read, and indistinguishable from one deferred last week.
--
-- reading_deferrals is a table of its own. Rejected: a source_scans row (its file_sha256 and text_scope describe a
-- reading that HAPPENED; a deferral is the opposite fact); evidence_sources.data_capture_status (one value per source,
-- no date, no reason, and a column a data migration INSERTs); a new v_scan_ledger status (the pair stays owed until it
-- is read, and every gate that reads the ledger's statuses would change meaning). A deferral is DISCHARGED BY
-- DERIVATION, never by a write: the view below drops it when a full reading covers it.
--
-- v_deferred_acts is a cross-stage pointer view (CLAUDE.md section 3): it reads research (search_executions,
-- citation_mining), evidence (evidence_sources, source_scans, reading_deferrals) and judgment (term_adjudications,
-- observed_terms), plus base (base_parameters). Nothing reads it as a gate: what age makes a standing deferral a defect
-- is the owner's to say, and no threshold is stored or typed anywhere. The age query is
--   SELECT * FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE deferred_at < datetime('now', '-<N> days') ORDER BY deferred_at;

CREATE TABLE reading_deferrals (
    deferral_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- NULL: the whole-source catalogue reading is what is deferred.
    parameter_id        INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    reason              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (trim(reason) <> ''),
    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW v_deferred_acts AS
-- v_deferred_acts: every deferral that still STANDS, one row each, with the date it was first recorded.
--   kind                subject
--   search              the exec id, with its slug when it has one
--   mining              the mined ref_id and the slug
--   reading             the ref_id and the parameter (or the whole source)
--   adjudication        the observation id, its ref_id and its surface form
-- ref_id and parameter_id are the same facts as columns, so a writer asks "is this pair already deferred?" of this
-- view and cannot disagree with it (db.py defer-reading does). They are NULL where the kind has none.
-- deferred_at is the date the obligation was FIRST recorded (created_at), never the date a row was last written: a
-- re-deferral that reset the clock would hide an old obligation. An older search row carries only a date; every other
-- row, and any search logged now, a minute.
--
-- WHAT EACH ARM DROPS, and why (a standing deferral is one nothing has since discharged):
--   search        NOTHING. A search later run is a new row that names nothing it discharges, so every deferred
--                 search lists, including one whose cell a later search has since covered. Not derivable today.
--   mining        a row whose source's citation_mining_status is no longer 'deferred' (the owner's execution signal,
--                 2026-09-18: db.py log-mining --discharge-deferral clears the row and the status together). A row whose
--                 ref resolves to no evidence_sources row (a lead anchor) has no status to read and lists while its own
--                 deferred_reason stands. created_at is the ROW's: a row first written by a pass that ran and deferred
--                 later is dated from the pass.
--   reading       a deferral whose source is now superseded (the replacement is what is owed) or whose parameter is no
--                 longer active (the ledger drops it), and one a FULL reading dated at or after the deferral covers:
--                 for a parameter, the strongest covering reading v_scan_ledger names is full-scope; for a NULL
--                 parameter, any full catalogue reading. Dates are minute-resolution, so "at or after".
--   adjudication  an observation whose LATEST adjudication (highest adjudication_id, the rule alias and rename writers
--                 use) is not DEFERRED: a later judgment of any other outcome discharges it.
SELECT 'search' AS kind,
       'exec ' || se.exec_id || COALESCE(' ' || se.slug, '') AS subject,
       se.mined_ref_id AS ref_id,
       se.parameter_id AS parameter_id,
       se.deferred_reason AS reason,
       se.created_at AS deferred_at,
       se.created_by_session AS created_by_session
  FROM search_executions se
 WHERE se.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'mining',
       COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id) || ' ' || cm.slug,
       COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id),
       NULL,
       cm.deferred_reason,
       cm.created_at,
       cm.created_by_session
  FROM citation_mining cm
  LEFT JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id)
 WHERE cm.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
   AND (e.ref_id IS NULL OR e.citation_mining_status = 'deferred')
UNION ALL
SELECT 'reading',
       d.ref_id || ' ' || COALESCE('parameter ' || d.parameter_id, 'whole source'),
       d.ref_id,
       d.parameter_id,
       d.reason,
       d.created_at,
       d.created_by_session
  FROM reading_deferrals d
  JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = d.ref_id AND e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
 WHERE (d.parameter_id IS NULL
        OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM base_parameters p
                    WHERE p.parameter_id = d.parameter_id AND p.status = 'active'))
   AND NOT EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM source_scans s
          WHERE s.ref_id = d.ref_id AND s.text_scope = 'full' AND s.created_at >= d.created_at
            AND CASE WHEN d.parameter_id IS NULL
                     THEN s.mode = 'catalogue'
                     ELSE s.scan_id = (SELECT l.scan_id FROM v_scan_ledger l
                                        WHERE l.ref_id = d.ref_id AND l.parameter_id = d.parameter_id
                                          AND l.text_scope = 'full') END)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'adjudication',
       'observation ' || o.observation_id || ' ' || o.ref_id || ' ' || o.surface_form,
       o.ref_id,
       NULL,
       a.rationale,
       a.created_at,
       a.created_by_session
  FROM term_adjudications a
  JOIN observed_terms o ON o.observation_id = a.observation_id
 WHERE a.outcome = 'DEFERRED'
   AND a.adjudication_id = (SELECT MAX(b.adjudication_id) FROM term_adjudications b
                             WHERE b.observation_id = a.observation_id);

PRAGMA user_version = 141;

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 BLOCKED            no full reading covers the pair AND the source carries an obstacle
--                        processing_blocked_reason (below): the full text could not be
--                        obtained or read, so the pair is not reading debt until a full
--                        reading is recorded. Any partial / fragment / abstract reading of
--                        the pair is still named in scan_id / text_scope / method.
--   5 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it, and no
--                        obstacle stands: the full text is obtainable and unread -- debt.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- WHY THIS ORDER (it is derived from what each fact proves; 122 ranked BLOCKED above every
-- reading and 123 below every reading, both guesses): a FULL reading proves the obstacle
-- gone, since the whole text was read, so 3 outranks 4. A partial, fragment or abstract
-- reading proves nothing about the full text, so under a standing obstacle 4 outranks 5.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id
-- (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1
-- and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading
-- recorded; 3 wins over the rest because a full reading supersedes a partial one.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read", and
-- this header is the ONE HOME of the classification of every processing_blocked_reason
-- value (evidence_sources CHECK, migration 091); each value appears here as a bare token
-- under exactly one head, and a test derives the CHECK and fails on a value this header
-- does not name. The writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. NOTHING
-- CLEARS THE COLUMN: it is the retrieval record and stays as history; the ledger alone says
-- whether a pair is still blocked.
--   obstacle to the text (BLOCKED, above):  no-full-text, paywalled, language.
--   copy of a typed fact (not an obstacle; the writers refuse it by pointer -- the judgement
--     lives in db.py _BLOCK_REASON_COPIES): no-quantified-claims -> a recorded full reading;
--     superseded -> superseded_by_ref_id.
--   pending owner question 8 of the round-3 adjudication, treated as NULL (the source owes
--     its reading): out-of-scope, tier-not-required (they say no text was unobtainable);
--     no-doi, not-indexed (migration 091's comments describe discovery -- "no resolvable
--     identifier for automated paths", "absent from the indexes the pipeline queries" --
--     not an obstacle to a text in hand, and a URL-only report admitted without a DOI can
--     be read).
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id
CREATE TABLE source_scans (
    -- AUTOINCREMENT, as 076 did for the other ids a record names: a scan_id is cited by
    -- session records and must never come to mean a different reading.
    scan_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- catalogue: every active parameter up to catalogue_version.
    -- targeted:  one parameter, target_parameter_id (a back-fill reading).
    mode                TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('catalogue', 'targeted')),
    catalogue_version   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (catalogue_version >= 1),
    target_parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- full: the whole document. partial: some pages of it. fragment: one page or clause
    -- of a larger instrument. abstract: an abstract or metadata record only.
    text_scope          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (text_scope IN
                                ('full', 'partial', 'fragment', 'abstract')),
    pages_read          INTEGER CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read >= 0),
    pages_total         INTEGER CHECK (pages_total IS NULL OR pages_total >= 1),
    -- Which saved file was read, by checksum: the manifest's own sha256 of the bytes.
    file_sha256         TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(file_sha256) = 64),
    -- Whether the open pass (quantities the catalogue lacks, plan section 3.4) was done
    -- in this reading.
    open_pass_done      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (open_pass_done IN (0, 1)),
    -- full-read: the text was read against the list. pre-screen: only a script listed
    -- where catalogue terms occur -- weaker, and v_scan_ledger says which it was.
    method              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('full-read', 'pre-screen')),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    CHECK ((mode = 'targeted' AND target_parameter_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR (mode = 'catalogue' AND target_parameter_id IS NULL)),
    CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_total IS NULL OR pages_read <= pages_total),
    -- "full" over a paged text means every page; a reading of fewer pages is partial.
    CHECK (text_scope <> 'full' OR pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read = pages_total)
)

            d = pathlib.Path(rl79.LOG_ROOT) / "session_fixture_t079"
            d.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            txt = d / f"{ref}-{mode}-{scope}-text.txt"
            txt.write_text("[PDF page 1 of 1]\nTASK-FIXTURE T079 reading text.\n")
            rl79.record_file(txt, "session_fixture_t079", f"{ref}-payload.json", purpose="fixture text",
                             ref_id=ref, kind="text-extraction")
            rl79._ARTEFACT_INDEX.clear()
            return db.record_scan({"ref_id": ref, "mode": mode, "target_parameter_id": target, "text_scope": scope,
                                   "file_sha256": hashlib.sha256(txt.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                                   "method": "full-read", "notes": "TASK-FIXTURE T079"}, session=S)

        def vq(sql, *params):
            """Rows, or None when the SQL cannot run (an absent view must turn a case red, not crash the run)."""
            try:
                return q(sql, *params)
            except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
                print(f"      DEFECT: {exc}")
                return None

        def standing(kind, ref=None, pid=None):
            return vq("SELECT kind, ref_id, parameter_id, reason, deferred_at, created_by_session "
                      "FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind=? AND ref_id IS ? AND parameter_id IS ?", kind, ref, pid)

        def n_def():
            return q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reading_deferrals")[0][0]

        def defer(ref, pid, reason="TASK-FIXTURE T079: owed, not read yet", dry=False):
            return refusal(db.defer_reading, ref, pid, reason, S, dry_run=dry)

        P79 = [r[0] for r in q("SELECT parameter_id FROM base_parameters WHERE status='active' ORDER BY 1")]
        PA, PB, PRET = P79[0], P79[1], P79[-1]
        R1, R2, R3, R4, R5 = (src79(x) for x in ("one", "two", "three", "four", "five"))

        # ── T079-01 (AT-17): the kinds list together, and an age window keeps the old rows and drops the new ──
        cli = run_cli("defer-reading", "--ref-id", R1, "--parameter", str(PA),
                      "--reason", "TASK-FIXTURE T079: the full text is owed", "--session", S)
        kinds = dict(vq("SELECT kind, COUNT(*) FROM v_deferred_acts GROUP BY 1") or [])
        aged = dict(vq("SELECT kind, COUNT(*) FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE deferred_at < datetime('now', '-1 days') "
                       "GROUP BY 1") or [])
        live_search = q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NOT NULL")[0][0]
        record("T079-01", "defer-reading lands through argparse; the view lists search, mining and reading, and "
               "an age window excludes the new reading and keeps the older rows",
               cli.returncode == 0 and kinds.get("reading") == 1 and kinds.get("search") == live_search
               and kinds.get("mining", 0) > 0 and aged.get("search") == live_search
               and aged.get("mining") == kinds.get("mining") and "reading" not in aged,
               f"rc={cli.returncode} {cli.stderr[:200]!r} kinds={kinds} aged={aged}")
        got = standing("reading", R1, PA)
        record("T079-06", "the new reading row carries its reason, session, and ref and parameter as columns",
               bool(got) and got[0][3].startswith("TASK-FIXTURE T079") and got[0][5] == S
               and q("SELECT status FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE ref_id=? AND parameter_id=?", R1, PA)[0][0] == "NOT-READ",
               f"{got} (the pair stays owed in the ledger)")

        # ── T079-02: every refusal fires, names its ground, and writes nothing ──
        n0 = n_def()
        retired_was = q("SELECT status FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?", PRET)[0][0]
        w("UPDATE base_parameters SET status='retired' WHERE parameter_id=?", PRET)      # HAND: a retired parameter
        R_OLD, R_NEW = src79("tombstone"), src79("successor")
        w("UPDATE evidence_sources SET superseded_by_ref_id=? WHERE ref_id=?", R_NEW, R_OLD)   # HAND: a tombstone
        scan79(R5, "full")                                  # R5 is fully read: nothing is owed on any pair
        scan79(R4, "full", "targeted", PA)                  # R4: only PA is covered by a full reading
        scan79(R3, "partial")                               # R3: a partial reading covers nothing
        con79 = sqlite3.connect(DB)
        unminted = dbcore.next_ref_id(con79)
        con79.close()
        m = {
            "blank": defer(R2, PA, "   "),
            "no such source": defer(unminted, PA),
            "superseded": defer(R_OLD, PA),
            "retired parameter": defer(R2, PRET),
            "no such parameter": defer(R2, PRET + 1000),
            "pair covered": defer(R4, PA),
            "whole source covered": defer(R5, None),
            "pair covered by a catalogue reading": defer(R5, PB),
            "same pair twice": defer(R1, PA),
        }
        w("UPDATE base_parameters SET status=? WHERE parameter_id=?", retired_was, PRET)
        need = {"blank": "reason", "no such source": "not an admitted source", "superseded": "superseded",
                "retired parameter": "retired", "no such parameter": "no such parameter",
                "pair covered": "full reading", "whole source covered": "full reading",
                "pair covered by a catalogue reading": "full reading", "same pair twice": "already"}
        bad = {k: m[k] for k, v in m.items() if not (v and v.startswith("defer-reading:") and need[k] in v)}
        record("T079-02", "defer-reading refuses a blank reason, an unknown or superseded source, a retired or "
               "unknown parameter, a pair a full reading covers and a second standing deferral, naming each ground",
               not bad and n_def() == n0, f"unrefused or unnamed: {bad} rows {n0}->{n_def()}")
        cli2 = run_cli("defer-reading", "--ref-id", R2, "--parameter", str(PA), "--reason", " ", "--session", S)
        record("T079-07", "through argparse a refusal exits non-zero with stderr starting REFUSING:",
               cli2.returncode != 0 and cli2.stderr.startswith("REFUSING:"), f"{cli2.returncode} {cli2.stderr[:120]!r}")
        # what is NOT refused: a partial reading covers nothing, a targeted full reading covers only its target,
        # and a whole-source deferral is allowed while any pair is owed
        ok_partial, ok_other_pair, ok_whole = defer(R3, PA), defer(R4, PB), defer(R4, None)
        record("T079-08", "a partial reading, an uncovered pair of a partly read source and the whole source "
               "(NULL parameter) of a source with owed pairs are all deferrable",
               ok_partial is None and ok_other_pair is None and ok_whole is None and n_def() == n0 + 3,
               f"{ok_partial!r} {ok_other_pair!r} {ok_whole!r} rows {n0}->{n_def()}")
        twice_whole = defer(R4, None)
        record("T079-17", "a second standing whole-source deferral (NULL parameter) is refused like a second pair",
               twice_whole is not None and twice_whole.startswith("defer-reading:") and "already" in twice_whole,
               f"{twice_whole!r}")
        n1 = n_def()
        dry = defer(R2, PA, dry=True)
        record("T079-09", "--dry-run writes nothing", dry is None and n_def() == n1, f"{dry!r}")

        # ── T079-03: the discharge is derived from a reading, never a write ──
        listed_first = bool(standing("reading", R3, PA))
        scan79(R3, "partial")
        still_partial = bool(standing("reading", R3, PA))
        scan79(R3, "full", "targeted", PB)
        still_other = bool(standing("reading", R3, PA))
        scan79(R3, "full", "targeted", PA)
        gone = not standing("reading", R3, PA)
        kept = q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reading_deferrals WHERE ref_id=? AND parameter_id=?", R3, PA)[0][0] == 1
        record("T079-03", "a partial reading does not discharge; a full reading of another parameter does not; "
               "a full reading of the pair does, and the deferral row stays as history",
               listed_first and still_partial and still_other and gone and kept,
               f"{listed_first} {still_partial} {still_other} {gone} {kept}")
        before_whole = bool(standing("reading", R4, None))
        scan79(R4, "partial")                               # a partial catalogue reading is not a full one
        partial_only = bool(standing("reading", R4, None))
        scan79(R4, "full", "targeted", PB)                  # a full TARGETED reading is not a full catalogue reading
        targeted_only = bool(standing("reading", R4, None))
        scan79(R4, "full")                                  # R4's whole-source deferral: a full catalogue reading
        whole_gone = not standing("reading", R4, None)
        record("T079-10", "a whole-source deferral is discharged by a full catalogue reading, not by a partial "
               "one or a full targeted one", before_whole and partial_only and targeted_only and whole_gone,
               f"{before_whole} {partial_only} {targeted_only} {whole_gone}")
        # The date clause: a deferral dated AFTER an earlier full catalogue reading is a new obligation (a
        # parameter minted since the reading is unread). HAND: no verb writes it, because the pair-covered
        # refusal stops it while every active parameter is covered.
        w("INSERT INTO reading_deferrals (ref_id, parameter_id, reason, created_at, created_by_session) "
          "VALUES (?, NULL, 'TASK-FIXTURE T079 later obligation', '2999-01-01 00:00', ?)", R4, S)
        later = standing("reading", R4, None)
        w("INSERT INTO reading_deferrals (ref_id, parameter_id, reason, created_at, created_by_session) "
          "VALUES (?, NULL, 'TASK-FIXTURE T079 earlier obligation', '2000-01-01 00:00', ?)", R4, S)
        both = standing("reading", R4, None)
        record("T079-11", "a deferral dated after the last full reading stands, one dated before it is discharged, "
               "and the two are not double counted",
               len(later or []) == 1 and later[0][4] == "2999-01-01 00:00" and len(both or []) == 1,
               f"{later} {both}")
        # a later state change takes a deferral out: a superseded source (its replacement is owed), a retired parameter
        w("UPDATE evidence_sources SET superseded_by_ref_id=? WHERE ref_id=?", R_NEW, R1)       # HAND: after the deferral
        gone_super = not standing("reading", R1, PA)
        w("UPDATE evidence_sources SET superseded_by_ref_id=NULL WHERE ref_id=?", R1)
        w("UPDATE base_parameters SET status='retired' WHERE parameter_id=?", PA)               # HAND: after the deferral
        gone_ret = not standing("reading", R1, PA)
        w("UPDATE base_parameters SET status='active' WHERE parameter_id=?", PA)
        back = bool(standing("reading", R1, PA))
        record("T079-12", "a deferral whose source is later superseded, or whose parameter is later retired, no "
               "longer lists (neither is owed), and lists again when the state is undone",
               gone_super and gone_ret and back, f"{gone_super} {gone_ret} {back}")

        # ── T079-04: a mining deferral is discharged by log-mining, read from the owner's execution signal ──
        mine = q("SELECT cm.slug, COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id) FROM citation_mining cm "
                 "JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id) "
                 "WHERE cm.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL AND e.citation_mining_status = 'deferred' ORDER BY 2 LIMIT 2")
        (SL1, MR1), (SL2, MR2) = mine[0], mine[1]
        mcount = lambda ref: vq("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='mining' AND ref_id=?", ref)[0][0]  # noqa: E731
        n_mine0 = vq("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='mining'")[0][0]
        dbl = mcount(MR1)
        # a pass that RAN without --discharge-deferral leaves the deferral standing (one column, two directions)
        out_a = db.log_mining(SL1, MR1, "backward", S, notes="TASK-FIXTURE T079: a pass that ran")
        after_a = mcount(MR1)
        db.log_mining(SL2, MR2, "backward", S, notes="TASK-FIXTURE T079: the pass that discharges",
                      discharge_deferral=True)
        after_b = mcount(MR2)
        n_mine1 = vq("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='mining'")[0][0]
        status_b = q("SELECT citation_mining_status FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?", MR2)[0][0]
        record("T079-04", "a mining deferral lists once; a pass without --discharge-deferral leaves it listed; "
               "log-mining --discharge-deferral takes it out, with the source's status 'mined'",
               dbl == 1 and after_a == 1 and after_b == 0 and n_mine1 == n_mine0 - 1 and status_b == "mined"
               and bool(out_a.get("deferral_still_standing")),
               f"{dbl} {after_a} {after_b} {n_mine0}->{n_mine1} {status_b} {out_a}")
        w("UPDATE evidence_sources SET citation_mining_status='mined' WHERE ref_id=?", MR1)     # HAND: the signal alone
        sig = mcount(MR1)
        w("UPDATE evidence_sources SET citation_mining_status='deferred' WHERE ref_id=?", MR1)
        record("T079-13", "the status 'mined' on the source takes its mining deferral out whatever the row holds "
               "(the owner's execution signal, 2026-09-18)", sig == 0, f"{sig}")

        # a lead anchor (a ref that resolves in source_locators, not evidence_sources) has no status to read: its own
        # deferred_reason is the signal, so it lists (an inner join to evidence_sources would drop it silently)
        w("INSERT INTO citation_mining (slug, local_ref_id, global_ref_id, deferred_reason, created_at, created_by_session, "
          "updated_at, updated_by_session) VALUES (?, 'LEAD-T079', NULL, 'TASK-FIXTURE T079: a lead anchor', "
          "'2026-01-01 00:00', ?, '2026-01-01 00:00', ?)", A, S, S)
        lead = vq("SELECT kind, ref_id, deferred_at FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='mining' AND ref_id='LEAD-T079'")
        record("T079-16", "a deferred mining row whose ref is no evidence_sources row (a lead anchor) lists, dated from "
               "its row", lead == [("mining", "LEAD-T079", "2026-01-01 00:00")], f"{lead}")

        # ── T079-05: the adjudication arm lists an observation whose LATEST adjudication is DEFERRED ──
        LATEST79 = ("WITH l AS (SELECT a.* FROM term_adjudications a WHERE a.adjudication_id = "
                    "(SELECT MAX(adjudication_id) FROM term_adjudications b WHERE b.observation_id = a.observation_id)) ")
        pick = q(LATEST79 + "SELECT observation_id FROM l WHERE outcome='DEFERRED' ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1")
        if not pick:                                        # HAND (TASK-FIXTURE): adjudicate one DEFERRED on the copy
            obs0 = q("SELECT observation_id FROM observed_terms ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1")[0][0]
            db.adjudicate_term(obs0, "DEFERRED", "TASK-FIXTURE T079: held", S)
            pick = [(obs0,)]
        OB = pick[0][0]
        row = vq("SELECT kind, ref_id, reason, deferred_at, created_by_session, subject FROM v_deferred_acts "
                 "WHERE kind='adjudication' AND subject LIKE ?", f"%observation {OB} %")
        lat = q(LATEST79 + "SELECT rationale, created_at, created_by_session FROM l WHERE observation_id=?", OB)[0]
        o_ref, o_form = q("SELECT ref_id, surface_form FROM observed_terms WHERE observation_id=?", OB)[0]
        n_adj = vq("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='adjudication'")[0][0]
        n_adj_expect = q(LATEST79 + "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM l WHERE outcome='DEFERRED'")[0][0]
        TERMX = q("SELECT term_id FROM terms ORDER BY term_id LIMIT 1")[0][0]
        db.adjudicate_term(OB, "NAMES-EXISTING", "TASK-FIXTURE T079: settled", S, term_id=TERMX)
        gone_adj = not vq("SELECT 1 FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='adjudication' AND subject LIKE ?",
                          f"%observation {OB} %")
        # the reverse order: an older settled judgment and a newer DEFERRED one lists
        db.adjudicate_term(OB, "DEFERRED", "TASK-FIXTURE T079: re-opened", S)
        reopened = vq("SELECT reason FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='adjudication' AND subject LIKE ?",
                      f"%observation {OB} %")
        record("T079-05", "an observation whose latest adjudication is DEFERRED lists with its source, surface form, "
               "rationale, date and session; a later adjudication of another outcome takes it out; a newer DEFERRED "
               "over an older outcome lists; 'DEFERRED' is in the column's CHECK",
               len(row or []) == 1 and row[0][1] == o_ref and row[0][2] == lat[0] and row[0][3] == lat[1]
               and row[0][4] == lat[2] and o_form in row[0][5] and n_adj == n_adj_expect and gone_adj
               and bool(reopened) and reopened[0][0] == "TASK-FIXTURE T079: re-opened"
               and "DEFERRED" in dbcore.check_values(sqlite3.connect(DB), "term_adjudications", "outcome"),
               f"{row} {lat} {n_adj}/{n_adj_expect} gone={gone_adj} reopened={reopened}")

        # two judgments in the SAME minute (created_at is minute-resolution): the higher adjudication_id governs
        db.adjudicate_term(OB, "NAMES-EXISTING", "TASK-FIXTURE T079: settled again, same minute", S, term_id=TERMX)
        tie = vq("SELECT 1 FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='adjudication' AND subject LIKE ?", f"%observation {OB} %")
        record("T079-18", "an observation judged DEFERRED and then settled in the same minute does not list (the "
               "higher id governs, not the date)", tie == [], f"{tie}")
        # a search that names no slug (a parameter, or a mined source) is deferred too, and lists
        db.log_search(slug=None, parameter_id=PA, language="EN", query_text="TASK-FIXTURE T079: a slug-less search",
                      engine="manual", depth_method="scoping", session=S, deferred_reason="TASK-FIXTURE T079: held",
                      prior_expectation="fixture prior, written before the call")
        slugless = vq("SELECT kind, parameter_id, reason FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind='search' AND parameter_id=?", PA)
        record("T079-19", "a deferred search naming no slug lists, with its parameter",
               slugless == [("search", PA, "TASK-FIXTURE T079: held")], f"{slugless}")

        # merge-parameter finds every table holding a parameter_id from the live schema and REFUSES one with no notes
        # column unless it is argued into _MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY: reading_deferrals must be, or a deferral blocks a merge
        def merge_try(fa, into):
            try:
                return db.merge_parameter(fa, into, "TASK-FIXTURE T079", S, dry_run=True)
            except Refusal as exc:
                return str(exc)
        pair79 = next(((fa, into) for fa in P79 for into in P79 if fa != into
                       and isinstance(merge_try(fa, into), dict)), None)     # two active parameters with no live work
        merge79 = None
        if pair79:
            R6 = src79("six")
            defer(R6, pair79[0], "TASK-FIXTURE T079: a deferral on the folded parameter")
            merge79 = merge_try(*pair79)
        record("T079-20", "merge-parameter is not blocked by a reading deferral on the folded parameter: the rows are "
               "kept as history (no notes column to move them with)",
               isinstance(merge79, dict) and "reading_deferrals.parameter_id" in merge79["kept_as_history"],
               f"{merge79}")

        # ── T079-14: the arms agree with the tables they read (derived, never typed), and no row lists twice ──
        arms = dict(vq("SELECT kind, COUNT(*) FROM v_deferred_acts GROUP BY 1") or [])
        want_search = q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NOT NULL")[0][0]
        want_adj = q(LATEST79 + "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM l WHERE outcome='DEFERRED'")[0][0]
        rows_total = vq("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_deferred_acts")[0][0]
        distinct = vq("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT kind, subject, deferred_at FROM v_deferred_acts)")[0][0]
        record("T079-14", "the search and adjudication arms count what their tables hold, and no row is listed twice",
               arms.get("search") == want_search and arms.get("adjudication") == want_adj and rows_total == distinct,
               f"{arms} search={want_search} adj={want_adj} total={rows_total} distinct={distinct}")
        record("T079-15", "reading_deferrals is in dbcore.writable_tables (the capture path sees it)",
               "reading_deferrals" in dbcore.writable_tables(sqlite3.connect(DB)), "")
finally:
    shutil.rmtree(TMP, ignore_errors=True)

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print(f"EXAMINED: {len(results)} assertion(s)")
print(f"RESULTS: {sum(results)}/{len(results)} tests passed")
if sum(results) < len(results):
    print(f"FAILED: {len(results) - sum(results)}")
print("=" * 70)
sys.exit(0 if results and all(results) else 1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""db.py's amendment writers from batch 20: every refusal proven to fire, and the
legitimate shape proven to pass.

WHY THIS EXISTS, as CLAUDE.md section 8 requires. db.py's Act-2 banner says "every refusal
here has a selftest case proving it fires AND a case proving the legitimate shape still
passes". Batch 20 (2026-09-25) added link-admission, amend-population-match, amend-term and
resolve-candidate --suggested-slug with no case at all, and a review that simply RAN them
found five defects no gate had seen:
  * link-admission refused a second admitting search, which log-search permits;
  * link-admission left results_admitted behind its own edges (exec 90 read 0 with 1 edge);
  * amend-term could never detect an unchanged scope_note, and nested each audit line
    inside the next;
  * --suggested-slug accepted a MERGED slug and a REHOME pointing at its own origin, and
    could not be required, so REHOME rows could still name no destination;
  * dbcore.fold_ref upper-cased the mixed-case Co1-NN namespace, so every writer that
    folds a ref id would have refused a genuine Co1 source.
What reaches the guidebook without these cases: a wrong provenance edge nothing can remove,
a coverage view that under-counts what searches yielded, a candidate "rehomed" nowhere, a
Co1 source that cannot be graded -- each looking fine to every gate.

Section D (migration 101, GAP-061's prerequisite) holds `decline-parameter` and the one
refusal it adds to `add-parameter` to the same standard. What reaches the guidebook
without it: a term judged NOT to be a design parameter minted as one anyway, so
extractions and determinations can key on a concept somebody already ruled out.

Section S (GAP-058) holds `add-source --slug` to "refuse before any write": a refused
admission used to leave its source and author rows committed, an orphan that is either
shipped or deleted by hand. It also holds `link-source-slug --local-ref-id`, the only way to
file into a slug whose labels mix schemes, and the refusal of a label another source holds.

Section X (GAP-060) holds `supersede-source`: without it a source admitted twice (a mirror,
a DOI-less re-entry) is gathered twice by the determination engine, and D04 stays red with
hand SQL as the only remedy. It proves D04 goes quiet on a fixture collision, that a live
determination blocks the move until it is retired, that the UPDATE reaches the capture
path, and that add-extraction, observe-term and add-population-match then refuse the
superseded source, whose rows the engine would drop.

Section C (GAP-055) holds `close-adversarial-pass`'s artefact parse: a SURVIVED artefact
written as a citation ("<file> page 15", "<file> (and the other 11)") used to make a
good-faith pass unclosable, so its audit stayed red for a pass that had done its work. A
path that escapes the repo must still refuse, and cited paths that do not resolve must stay
visible. The verb's --help must name the 2026-09-27 ruling that holds pass 1 open, and a
finding admitted only on the database file is closed but reported, because the database is
not an artefact of attack.

Section E (I1) holds `amend-source --field evidence_type`: without it a source filed at the
wrong rung of the ladder (a Co-1/T6 contradiction, a grey report typed as a trial) keeps
anchoring at the wrong strength, because the only correction was hand SQL. It proves the
tier moves with the type by derivation only, that a move to co1 needs the D-0178 warrant
and a co1_source_type from schemas.enums.Co1SourceType (grain_for grades a Co-1 source's
grain from it), that a move off co1 keeps the old warrant in the ledger and NULLs the
Co-1-only columns, and that a source a live determination rests on cannot move.

Section K (I8, GAP-005) holds `update-code-lead` and add-code-lead's near-duplicate refusal:
without the verb R15 cannot be discharged against a lead, so a lead whose document was
retrieved stays REFERENCE-ONLY and its note keeps asserting what the document was found not
to say. It proves the move is ledgered and append-only (a note that is only a substring of
the held notes is still appended), that the refusal's "update that row instead" names a
command that works, and that the duplicate key folds case and punctuation
without erasing a Korean or Japanese name.

Section J (I7) holds the declared jurisdiction vocabulary at write time: without it every
writer took any string, so an undeclared code (`PT` on batch 23's branch) reached the corpus
and the blocking `jurisdiction_db_vocabulary` audit found it only after it landed. It proves
an undeclared code, the ruled rejected spelling and a case variant are refused by each
writer of a gated table, that a code admitted in the same change is accepted, that every
value live in a gated table still passes (the refusal mirrors the audit and is not stricter),
and that the audit is green on the copy after the writers ran.

Runs on a COPY of the canonical database in a temp directory (dbcore refuses to open the

sanctioned CLI, every row the skill says is refused: a `verified` extraction over an

recorded, a fabricated claim text behind a false `--verbatim-exempt`, a numerical row with
no locator, a `full` reading of a publisher landing page, a parameter direction with the
rationale "no admitted source read", a term minted beside its near-duplicate, a NAMES-NEW
adjudication to an existing term, a harm finding with no `insufficient` edge, a connection

_PRAGMA_UV = re.compile(r"^\s*PRAGMA\s+user_version\s*=\s*(\d+)", re.I)
_BLOCK_COMMENT = re.compile(r"/\*.*?\*/", re.S)


def _split_statements(sql: str) -> list:
    """Split a migration body into individual statements.

    Uses sqlite3.complete_statement, which is quote-, comment- and
    CREATE TRIGGER-aware: a semicolon inside a string literal, inside a comment,
    or inside a trigger body does not end a statement. A naive split(';') would
    desync on a source title containing a semicolon, which this corpus can carry.
    """
    out, buf = [], ""
    for line in sql.splitlines(keepends=True):
        buf += line
        if sqlite3.complete_statement(buf):
            if buf.strip():
                out.append(buf.strip())
            buf = ""
    if buf.strip():
        out.append(buf.strip())
    return out


def _code_of(chunk: str) -> str:
    """The chunk with comments removed, for CLASSIFICATION only.

    A statement is buffered together with any comment lines preceding it -- a
    comment is not a complete statement, so it accumulates until real SQL closes
    the chunk. Every migration in this repository opens with a comment header,
    so the first chunk of a wrapped file is literally
    "-- Generated: ...\nBEGIN TRANSACTION;". Matching the raw chunk against
    ^BEGIN therefore fails and the wrapper survives, which is how the runner
    ended up starting a transaction inside a transaction. Classify on this;
    execute the original, where the comments are harmless.
    """
    text = _BLOCK_COMMENT.sub("", chunk)
    return "\n".join(l for l in text.splitlines()
                      if l.strip() and not l.strip().startswith("--")).strip()


def _is_noop(chunk: str) -> bool:
    """True if the chunk is only comments/whitespace and must not be executed."""
    return not _code_of(chunk).strip(";").strip()

"""Mutation harness for T-079 critic repairs. View mutations patch the scratch copy of the database the test makes;
db.py / test-visible mutations patch scripts/db.py in place and restore it from a backup."""
import json, os, pathlib, re, shutil, sqlite3, subprocess, sys, textwrap

REPO = pathlib.Path('/home/user/guidebook/.claude/worktrees/agent-a4fe8dcfc29947db2')
TEST = REPO / 'scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py'
TEST2 = REPO / 'scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py'
DBPY = REPO / 'scripts/db.py'
BACKUP = pathlib.Path('/tmp/claude-0/t079r/db.py.orig')

SHIM = textwrap.dedent('''
    import sys, shutil, sqlite3, runpy, json
    spec = json.loads(sys.argv[1]); test = sys.argv[2]
    orig = shutil.copy
    def cp(src, dst, *a, **k):
        r = orig(src, dst, *a, **k)
        if str(dst).endswith('guidebook.db'):
            c = sqlite3.connect(dst)
            sql = c.execute("select sql from sqlite_master where name=?", (spec['view'],)).fetchone()[0]
            assert spec['old'] in sql, 'mutation target not found: ' + spec['old'][:60]
            c.execute('DROP VIEW ' + spec['view'])
            c.execute(sql.replace(spec['old'], spec['new'], 1))
            c.commit(); c.close()
        return r
    shutil.copy = cp
    sys.argv = [test]
    runpy.run_path(test, run_name='__main__')
''')


def run(cmd):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    fails = re.findall(r'\[✗\] (\S+):', r.stdout)
    return r.returncode, fails


def view_mut(mid, view, old, new, tests=(TEST,)):
    out = []
    for t in tests:
        rc, f = run([sys.executable, '-c', SHIM, json.dumps({'view': view, 'old': old, 'new': new}), str(t)])
        out += f if rc else []
        if rc and not f:
            out.append('(crash rc=%d)' % rc)
    return mid, out


def py_mut(mid, old, new, tests=(TEST, TEST2), file=DBPY):
    src = BACKUP.read_text() if file == DBPY else file.read_text()
    assert old in src, f'{mid}: target not found: {old[:70]!r}'
    file.write_text(src.replace(old, new, 1))

CREATE TABLE gap_mining (
    gap_mining_id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    gap_id               TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES gaps(gap_id),

    -- Provenance
    created_at           TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session TEXT NOT NULL,

    -- Search strategy record (replayable). JSON:
    --   {"strategies": [{"tool":"pubmed","query":"...","date_filter":"...",
    --                    "tier_filter":"...","connectors_used":["pubmed",...],
    --                    "candidates_returned":N}, ...]}
    search_strategy_record TEXT NOT NULL,
    candidates_returned    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    candidates_reviewed    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

    -- Outcome enum
    outcome              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(outcome IN (
        'closure_evidence_found',  -- enough to close the gap (rule #7 must fire)
        'partial_evidence_found',  -- some discoveries; gap stays OPEN with annotation
        'null_result',             -- searches ran clean, no relevant discoveries
        'gap_recategorized',       -- gap not mining-addressable after all
        'deferred'                 -- connectors unavailable / other blocker
    )),

    -- Discoveries: JSON array of evidence_sources.ref_id values written to
    -- evidence_sources + source_slug_links as part of THIS attempt.
    -- NULL or '[]' permitted for null_result / deferred / gap_recategorized.
    discoveries_logged   TEXT,

    -- Rule #10 gate: candidates returned but not yet verified are recorded
    -- as DOIs only, NOT INSERTed to evidence_sources. The next session may
    -- verify and promote them. Mirrors supersession_check.superseding_dois.
    candidate_dois       TEXT,  -- JSON array

    -- Method used. Composite is the cluster-search pattern (skills/
    -- supersession-audit_SKILL.md §3) — 3-6 queries per gap, evaluated
    -- as a single attempt rather than per-query.
    check_method         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(check_method IN (
        'pubmed_cluster',
        'scholar_gateway_lived_experience',
        'cochrane_direct',
        'standards_body_direct',
        'multilingual_research',
        'composite'
    )),

    notes                TEXT,

    -- Integrity: closure_evidence_found must have at least one discovery
    CHECK (
        outcome != 'closure_evidence_found'
        OR (discoveries_logged IS NOT NULL AND discoveries_logged != '[]')
    ),

    -- Integrity: gap_recategorized must document why (>=20 chars)
    CHECK (
        outcome != 'gap_recategorized'
        OR (notes IS NOT NULL AND length(notes) >= 20)
    ),

    -- Integrity: deferred must document the blocker (>=10 chars)
    CHECK (
        outcome != 'deferred'
        OR (notes IS NOT NULL AND length(notes) >= 10)
    )
)

definition.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
definition.description:
Withdraw a task suggestion you queued earlier with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion has gone stale: the issue was fixed in this session (by you or the user), it turned out not to be a problem after all, or you have queued a better-scoped replacement — in that case queue the replacement with spawn_task first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only a suggestion the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn. If they already started, dismissed or edited it, the result says so and nothing changes; that answer is final, so don't retry or re-flag it.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", don't start it anew, and do it here only if the user asks for that in chat.

reason.description: Optional short note on why the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34". It doesn't change the outcome.

task_id.description: The task_id from the spawn_task result that queued the suggestion (of the form task_1a2b3c4d).

definition.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
definition.description:
Suggest a separate task for something you noticed that is outside the scope of your current work.

Call this when you come across something that deserves fixing but doesn't belong in this change — dead code, stale docs, a missing test, a confirmed TODO, a bug or security issue spotted in passing. Don't use it for trivial fixes you can make inline, for anything the user asked you to do, for vague code-smell impressions or unverified hunches, or to split off parts of your own task. The call only queues a suggestion and returns; carry on with your current work.

The user sees a "Suggested task" card in the Claude desktop app with your title and tldr, can open the full prompt, and with one click starts it as a new session — on their machine in their local clone of this repository (optionally a fresh worktree of it), or in the cloud — sends it to this session, or dismisses it. A new session starts from your prompt alone, on a checkout that may not have this session's changes, so the prompt has to stand alone: what to change and why, the files involved by repository-relative path, and any context from this conversation it depends on. Absolute paths and other state of this environment may not exist there. If the find involves a secret or credential, say where it is rather than copying the value, since the prompt is stored and displayed.

The result carries a task_id; if the suggestion later becomes moot, withdraw it with dismiss_task.

prompt.description: The opening message of the new session: the goal, the files involved by repository-relative path, the context it needs from this conversation, and what done looks like. The user can read it in full before starting; markdown is fine. Keep it to what the task needs (hard limit 32000 characters) — the new session can read the code itself.

title.description: The card's heading and the new session's title: a short imperative phrase starting with a verb, under 60 characters, that makes sense on its own — e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option".

tldr.description: One or two plain sentences on what the task would do and why it is worth doing. Shown on the card under the title; it is what the user reads when deciding whether to start it, so no file paths or code.
